title: Apply Skill Thrift Principle to all WAI skills — lean primary files, reference files for verbose content

_behavior_directive.what_this_is: Epic to systematically slim every WAI skill file. Primary files carry behavioral instructions only. Verbose content (examples, schemas, deferred specs, onboarding prose, report templates) moves to secondary reference files loaded on-demand.
_behavior_directive.what_this_is_NOT: Not removing functionality. Every behavioral instruction is preserved. Only the token cost of loading the skill changes.

perceive: templates/commands/wai*.md — all skill files, sorted by size

execute.principle: Primary skill file = behavioral instructions only. No onboarding prose, no use-case catalogs, no JSON/bash examples the agent already knows, no descriptions of unimplemented features. Secondary {skill}-reference.md files in same folder carry reference material.

items.notes: Biggest skill. Schema examples, PEV chain examples, type system docs, lifecycle diagrams — most can move to reference
Backlog review protocol. Scoring rubrics, fit-check examples, priority tables — reference material

Already trimmed from 568. May have more to cut.

tier3_already_lean.description: Skills <100 lines — likely already lean, review only

per_skill_process: 2. Identify: onboarding prose, use-case catalogs, JSON/bash examples, report templates, deferred/unimplemented features
3. Write slimmed primary file preserving all behavioral instructions
4. Write {skill}-reference.md with moved content (only if content has value — don't create empty reference files)

verify: Every skill's primary file contains all behavioral instructions (no behavior lost)
Reference files exist only where verbose content was moved
Template spoke skills are in sync with templates/commands/
Total token savings reported per tier
estimated_savings: Tier 1 alone: ~15,000-20,000 tokens. Full epic: ~25,000+ tokens across all skills.
